title: Freya and the Compass
premise: When mountain guide Lior Dunmore pulls a sealed chest from a flooded river, he finds a compass that points not north but toward the wreck of the Meridian Star, a salvage vessel sunk under disputed waters belonging to a nation that no longer exists. The chest's seal marks him as heir to a claim the old regime buried, and both a ruthless salvage fleet and an exiled archivist who claims the compass belongs to her people will stop at nothing to reach it first. Racing six tides ahead of the monsoon, Lior must decide whether to sell his find, surrender it, or use it to force a reckoning for the drowned village the fleet destroyed years ago. In the end he scuttles the fleet's flagship in the wreck's lagoon, hands the compass to the exiles' council, and walks into the mountains finally carrying a name he chose himself.
about_author: Yara Whitlock is a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people the maps forgot, from a cabin she shares with a one-eared dog named Sextant.

chapters.title: The River Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: Lior, guiding a last client before the season closes, drags a brass-stamped chest from a flood-scoured bank. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: wary curiosity — the wilderness has never handed him anything for free.

chapters.title: A Seal for a Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Lior pries the chest open: documents, coin, and a compass whose needle ignores north. A black-market appraiser recognizes the dead nation's seal and tells him to burn it. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: dread — he knows what it means when men whisper instead of bargain.

chapters.title: Men Who Don't Knock
chapters.summary: Salvage fleet enforcers ransack Lior's cabin; he escapes through a storm drain with the compass but loses everything else. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: cold fury — they took his gear, but worse, they made him prey.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Nadia Voss, exiled cartographer of the drowned nation, finds Lior and claims the compass is her people's patrimony, stolen by the Meridian Star's captain. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: guarded hope — two liars measuring each other's truths.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Nadia decodes the chest's charts: the wreck lies in a lagoon reachable only at low tide, and monsoon landfall closes the window in six days. The fleet departs tonight. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Stowaway Water
chapters.summary: Lior and Nadia smuggle aboard a coastal freighter; Lior's blacklist means every port official is a threat. They are nearly caught by a customs sweep. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the old shame of being a man without papers, and the new comfort of not being alone in it.

chapters.title: What the Fleet Drowned
chapters.summary: In a port tavern, a retired deckhand describes how the fleet sank a village to cover its looting of the Meridian Star — Nadia's home. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; this stopped being about treasure.

chapters.title: The First Tide
chapters.summary: The pair steal a skiff and run the reef passage at slack water, nearly swamped by a rogue swell. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: exhilaration — for once the wilderness is testing him on his own terms.

chapters.title: Compass Points
chapters.summary: Camped ashore, the compass needle steadies toward the lagoon only when Nadia holds it; Lior realizes it answers bloodline, not magnetism. He asks what else she hasn't told him. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: trust cracking under the weight of secrets.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Wake
chapters.summary: They discover the fleet has taken hostages from a fishing village to force pilots through the reef. Lior wants to run; Nadia refuses. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: the cost of justice outside the law — you can't save everyone and still arrive in time.

chapters.title: Second Tide, Bad Water
chapters.summary: A night crossing through a squall wrecks their water stores; Lior's guidecraft keeps them alive, and something unspoken settles between them. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: grudging tenderness born of shared competence.

chapters.title: The Turncoat Pilot
chapters.summary: A defected fleet navigator offers to guide them for a share, then tries to signal the fleet; Lior catches him mid-signal. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: bitter clarity — betrayal is just loyalty priced higher.

chapters.title: Halfway Tide
chapters.summary: Three tides left. Nadia reveals the compass was her father's, and the 'claim' in the chest names her family as rightful salvors — meaning she needs Lior less than she let him believe. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: guilt, and the fear that honesty will cost her the only ally she has.

chapters.title: Reef Ghosts
chapters.summary: Diving the outer reef to bypass a fleet picket, Lior finds the village's drowned boats moored in a silent row. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: awe curdling into anger; the sea keeps better records than any court.

chapters.title: Two Tides
chapters.summary: The fleet reaches the lagoon first and begins salvage operations under armed guard. Lior and Nadia watch from a sea cave, outgunned and out of time. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: despair — until he notices the fleet's dredge is cracking the reef itself.

chapters.title: The Wreck Speaks
chapters.summary: Nadia infiltrates the fleet's survey barge disguised as a supply runner and photographs the captain's log proving the village massacre. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: vindication that tastes like ash — proof means nothing without someone left to judge it.

chapters.title: One Tide
chapters.summary: Monsoon squalls build on the horizon. Lior proposes the impossible: sink the fleet's dredge in the lagoon channel, trapping the fleet inside the closing window. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: terror and certainty fused — the wilderness forgives nothing, so give it a reason to be merciless.

chapters.title: Sabotage at Slack Water
chapters.summary: Underwater cutting of the dredge's sea valves goes wrong; Lior is caught in a downflooding compartment and barely surfaces as the ship lists. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the calm of a man who has already decided the price is worth paying.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: Storm strikes. The trapped fleet fights its own hull while Lior and Nadia ride the last low tide into the lagoon and raise the wreck's claim beacon — legally sealing the site under the old nation's law, which the fleet's insurers still honor. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: chaos becoming leverage.

chapters.title: Judgment in the Lagoon
chapters.summary: With the fleet stranded and the evidence broadcast to maritime authorities, the fleet captain's own crew mutinies rather than face piracy charges. The hostages walk free. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, without a courtroom — exactly as promised.

chapters.title: What Belongs to the Drowned
chapters.summary: Nadia's exile council convenes aboard the half-submerged Meridian Star; the compass is returned, and the salvage rights fund the rebuilding of the village. She offers Lior a place among them. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: belonging offered, not begged for.

chapters.title: North, Finally
chapters.summary: Lior declines to stay but leaves with his record cleared and a letter naming him guide to the rebuilt coast. On the ridge above the lagoon, he checks an ordinary compass — it points north, and so does he. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; the man the rivers blacklisted finally has somewhere to return to.
